“I can see a better world on the horizon. I know the road to get there will be long, but it will not be lonely-because I know that we will walk it together”
My Name is Phara Souffrant Forrest. I am the daughter of first generation Haitian Americans, a Union Nurse, and a Democratic Socialist representing Brooklyn’s 57th District in Albany.

As the daughter of Haitian immigrants and a Black woman, I know what it means to feel racism and prejudice. As an organizer and legislator, I know the dignity and strength that comes from fighting back and the power of standing in solidarity against greed and injustice.

I believe in a simple vision: that life in this city does not need to be so hard. I am running for re-election to reform our inhuman criminal justice system, Abolish I.C.E. in New York, and win Universal Healthcare and Childcare in New York
THIS MOVEMENT NEEDS YOU!
What we're fighting for
Treatment Not Jail

For decades, New York State has funneled people experiencing mental health crises not towards treatment, but into our jails and prisons. Our jails have become the largest psychiatric treatment centers, and instead of receiving treatment, care, and rehabilitation, people face abuse that means they are more destabilized and traumatized when they leave than when they enter. This cycle must stop
Phara is championing the Treatment Court Expansion Act
in the Assembly to ensure that treatment, not jail, is the first option for someone facing a mental health crisis.
Abolish I.C.E. in New York

What would the 57th district be without our immigrant neighbors? We are a neighborhood that is made stronger by those who came here from Haiti, Bangladesh, Nigeria, and Mexico in search of a place where they could raise their children in peace and live a dignified life.

The Trump administration has given New York a choice: abandon our immigrant neighbors or face military occupation, violence in our streets, and massive cuts in federal funding. Phara will never abandon our immigrant neighbors. That is why she is fighting to end all collusion between New York State and ICE by passing New York for All.
Healthcare for All

As a nurse, Phara has seen firsthand how the private market, insurance companies, the pharmaceutical industry, and private hospitals profit from suffering. In order to ensure that all New Yorkers have the dignity of being able to seek medical treatment, we must pass the New York Health Act

which would create a single-payer healthcare system here in New York. Phara has also championed funding for safety net hospitals, rate increases for Medicaid, and state support for people impacted by the Trump administration’s cuts to healthcare coverage.
Housing is a Human Right

Every New Yorker has the right to a safe, stable and affordable place to live. Our current system is in the hands of a profit-driven real estate model that places financial speculation and profit over the dignity of a stable home. Phara believes that we must transform housing from a vehicle for individual profit into a collective, socially controlled good,
by creating a Social Housing Development Authority.
Ending Displacement
Phara became an organizer to stop a landlord from evicting her family and turning their apartment into luxury condos. She is fighting to build tenant
power by passing the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act and the REST Act.

Phara unequivocally believes all tenants should live without the fear of eviction when their lease comes up for renewal. She also supports a deed theft eviction moratorium to prevent the displacement of residents who are fighting to preserve their family homes.
Free CUNY and SUNY

Phara strongly believes in the necessity of expanding funding and resources for public education, and has been a champion of the New Deal for CUNY. She has also introduced the New Deal for SUNY, because she believes that higher education must be available, at no cost
, to all New Yorkers regardless of income.

As a proud graduate of SUNY Geneseo, CUNY SPS, and CUNY City Tech, Phara knows that our public schools are an exceptional resource which we must invest in and to which all New Yorkers must be given access.
But how do we pay for it? By Taxing the Rich
Phara believes in a simple idea that some would call radical: life in New York City does not need to be so hard.
Last year Billionaires in New York received a $12 Billion dollar tax cut. This is the largest single transfer of wealth in Human History

. While the billionaires get tax breaks the working majority of New York gets stuck with the tab. Our city is now facing a $5 billion budget crisis, our social services remain underfunded, and people are working longer hours, commuting farther, and making less than they ever have.
This is the result of a political choice to stand with the oligarchs and corporations over the working people who run this city. A choice Phara will never make.

In a city with 400,000 millionaires and over 60 billionaires, a budget deficit this severe is the result of a lack of political will, not a lack of funds. We know that the money is here, we just need politicians who are willing to stand up to the oligarchs and deliver for working people-like Phara
Phara believes we need politicians who are willing to make the wealthiest pay their fare share. It is time to Tax the Rich.
PEOPLE POWER THIS MOVEMENT
Phara has never taken a penny from corporate interests, fossil fuel companies, or those who profit from of deportations, weapons, and war—and she never will.
Phara’s campaign is 100% powered by hundreds of people just like you.
“A better world is possible”
“But you have to demand it, because power, is never given”
What We've Done

In Albany, Phara has been a steadfast champion for working people. She has cosponsored over 280 pieces of legislation and introduced six bills of her own, focusing on removing barriers to healthcare access and reuniting incarcerated New Yorkers with their families and communities. Her most notable accomplishments in Albany are the Invest in Our New York package of taxes on the wealthy and corporations, and her landmark parole justice reform, Less Is More.
Reformed our Cruel Parole System
Less Is More

Phara’s Less Is More legislation, which she passed in her first term, eliminated prison time for a number of minor technical parole violations. Because of this law, thousands of people who were incarcerated based on minor violations are no longer trapped in our carceral system.
Ended Copays on Insulin
Phara led the fight to eliminate insulin copays for all New York insurance plans in the 2024 state budget, saving New Yorkers $15 million a year in costs on a lifesaving medication
Green New Deal in New York
In 2023, New York passed the Build Public Renewables Act
, which authorized and directed the New York Power Authority to make historic investments to build publicly-owned, union made, renewable energy.
Grew our Movement by electing Zohran Mamdani as Mayor

Phara worked to turn out over 20,000 people to vote for Zohran in the 57th district, the most of any assembly district in the city. Phara and Zohran were elected to the Assembly as part of a slate in 2020, and she is proud to be working alongside him to deliver for working New Yorkers.
Taxed the Rich
During the 2021 legislative cycle, Phara was a lead supporter of the Invest in our New York

legislative package and a powerful part of the grassroots coalition. With her support and advocacy, the New York state budget adopted higher income taxes on wealthy individuals and corporations and raised a record $4.5 billion.
Won Historic Tenant Protections
Passed the Good Cause Eviction Law
which limited rent increases and requires extended and stricter justification before a landlord is allowed to evict a tenant.
Built Affordable Housing

Phara secured state funding for a 100% affordable housing development at 1024 Fulton Street, in partnership with Senator Jabari Brisport. This sustainable development will include 125 affordable units, a senior center, and a health clinic. 1024 Fulton Street exemplifies the need for social housing in New York – publicly owned, community controlled, sustainable, and affordable.
Invested in Our Community

Phara fought to win congestion pricing in Manhattan which raised half a billion dollars in revenue for public transit in the first year alone; including funding for signal upgrades on the A/C line and elevators at the Bedford-Nostrand G and Franklin Avenue 2/3/4/5. She also secured $410 million in funding to overhaul the
“Crown Heights Cluster”
at Franklin Avenue and Eastern Parkway.
Built People Power in the 57th District

Phara believes in using her office to support organizing. That’s why she started Brooklyn ROOTS to help residents of the 57th district develop and build the skills to advocate for change in their community. ROOTS participants spend four Saturdays sharing knowledge and covering topics including organizing, relationship-building, power mapping, state government 101, and the local context.
